questions.question: What does an `@`-prefixed folder like `@analytics` define in the App Router?
options: A private folder excluded from routing
A named parallel route slot that a layout can render alongside its normal children
questions.explanation: `@folderName` defines a slot, passed into the layout as a prop with that same name, rendered independently alongside `children`.

questions.question: Why does each parallel route slot need a `default.tsx`?
options: As a fallback for when the current URL doesn't match anything inside that specific slot
To define the slot's TypeScript types
It replaces the need for a layout.tsx
questions.explanation: Since slots render independently, Next.js needs a fallback (`default.tsx`) to render in a slot whose own routes don't match the current URL.

questions.question: In the intercepting routes folder convention, what does `(..)` mean compared to `(.)`?
options: They are identical in every way
`(.)` intercepts at the same level; `(..)` intercepts one level up, matching how far up the tree the real route lives
`(..)` is only valid in Pages Router, not App Router
questions.explanation: The number of dots mirrors relative path segments — more dots means intercepting a route that lives further up the folder tree.

questions.question: When a user pastes a direct URL to an intercepted route (e.g. a photo's URL) instead of clicking a link inside the app, what happens?
options: It always renders the modal version, even on a hard reload
It 404s, since intercepted routes replace the real page
It renders the real, full standalone page rather than the intercepted modal version
It redirects back to the grid
questions.explanation: The router only applies the intercepted (modal) version for client-side navigation originating from within the intercepting segment; a direct/hard navigation renders the actual standalone page.
